report.summary: Cause: in `ship()` in `public/src/store.js`, the store changed the order object in place and then called `set({ orders: state.orders })` with the same array. `set()` skips the update and the re-render when no value changed by reference, so the row kept saying "Packed" until a reload. Fix: after the server confirms, `ship()` now builds a new `orders` array. It replaces the matching row with `{ ...order, ...updated }` and clears the error. It looks the row up in the current state, so a list reload that lands during the update can't break it. The failure path is unchanged: the row keeps its status and "Could not update the order." is shown.
report.verification: `npm test` passes (4 of 4). I ran the registry check `orders-ship-updates-row` (checks/ship-steps.json) before and after the change. Before, it reported EXPECTATION_NOT_MET on `row-shows-shipped`. After, it completed with no problems. `compare_reports` returned IMPROVED: "1 problem gone (EXPECTATION_NOT_MET), none new." That covers one successful ship of the first packed order, on one run per side. I did not test the failure path or the other filters with Recovery Probe. `plan_verification` ran before I made any changes, so it proposed no checks. The suspect scanner also couldn't run because the `typescript` package isn't installed. I stopped only the server and browser-helper processes I started.
